items.followUp: Differentiate between a population and an ecosystem.

rubric.why: A population is made up of organisms of the same species living in a particular area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the single-species group and its area.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living together in an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the different species or populations living in the shared area.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area at a particular time.
A community consists of populations of different species living together in a particular area.

items.followUp: Write two differences between mitosis and meiosis.

rubric.why: Mitosis has one division and produces two daughter cells, while meiosis has two divisions and produces four daughter cells.
rubric.description: Compares the number of divisions or daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast between mitosis and meiosis in divisions or daughter-cell number.

rubric.why: Mitosis maintains chromosome number and produces genetically identical cells, whereas meiosis halves chromosome number and produces genetically varied cells.
rubric.description: Compares chromosome number or genetic similarity of the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in chromosome number or genetic similarity.

modelAnswer: Mitosis consists of one division and produces two daughter cells; meiosis consists of two divisions and produces four daughter cells.
Mitosis maintains the same chromosome number and produces genetically identical cells; meiosis halves the chromosome number and produces genetically varied cells.

items.followUp: What is crossing over, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Chiasmata are the points where non-sister chromatids cross and exchange genetic material.
rubric.description: Identifies chiasmata as the points of crossing over.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as crossing points or points of genetic-material exchange.

rubric.why: Chiasmata form between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I.
rubric.description: Identifies the chromatids or chromosomes involved, or the meiotic stage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes or prophase I.

modelAnswer: Chiasmata are the points where non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes cross over and exchange genetic material.
They form during prophase I of meiosis.
